content.title: Route per-kind Turn behavior through turnBehavior
content.intent: This PR refactors per-kind Turn behavior into one table, turnBehavior, and adds an architecture rule that blocks new kind branches outside it.

chapters.caption: One table decides what a Turn does
chapters.body: turnBehavior maps a Conversation kind, whether a person sent the input, and an Automation-run flag to one of four fixed behaviors: root, person in Thread, agent in child, or Automation run [1]. Each behavior lists delivery, prompt mode, the answer gate and tool access. The selector checks the Automation flag first, then kind, then the Source [2].
asks: Why is automationRun a flag and not a kind?
Is isPersonInput the same check as before?

chapters.caption: Callers read the table instead of agentInvocationId or declaresResult
chapters.body: The agent run builds the behavior once and uses it for the result gate [1]. The prompt no longer works out its own mode from the Run [2]. The tool registry reads turnTools for reportBlocked, noReply and the review desk [3]. Event delivery in the mailbox worker asks for location delivery instead of checking kind === "root" [4].
asks: Do subscriptions and user customization use the same swap?

chapters.caption: Agent tools bind in tool wiring, not in the runner
chapters.body: The runner used to bind spawnAgent and messageAgent from agentInvocationId [1]. Now it passes the binders on, and bindAgentTools uses the Turn's agents value with the same depth rule [2]. The Thread worker no longer disables subagents; a person's Thread Turn gets agents: "none" [3]. The CLI checks agents, not the invocation id [4].
asks: Can a too-deep child still message its parent?

chapters.caption: Tests pin the table and the binding
chapters.body: A unit test checks each kind and input pair against its expected behavior, including the Automation run [1]. Binding tests cover agents: "none", both agent modes, and the too-deep case [2]. An eval checks that a person's reply in an Automation run's thread is a normal chat Turn that delivers and does not call finishAutomationRun [3].
asks: Is there a test for an Event Turn on a Thread?

chapters.caption: Where the result is not identical
chapters.body: A child Run with no Conversation row now throws [1], and person input on a task throws [2]. Inference: an Event Turn on a Thread used to run with root tools and subagents turned off [3][4]. Now it falls into agent-in-child, so it gets child_agent prompts, reportBlocked, no review desk, and can spawn agents.

decisions.question: Can an Event or timer Turn run on a Thread? If so, should it get child-agent behavior and spawnAgent?
Is it confirmed that no path sends web or Slack input to a task Conversation, so the new throw cannot fire?

asks: Does the PR's no-behavior-change claim hold?
What happens to a root Turn that has an agentInvocationId?

chapters.caption: A source rule keeps new kind branches in one module
chapters.body: The architecture check now scans runtime source for kind comparisons, parent-edge truthiness, declaresResult reads and person-Source checks outside kind-behavior.ts [1]. Existing sites are listed in a baseline that can only go down [2]. Tests check which forms count as a branch and which do not [3].
asks: Will the regex miss aliased or wrapped branches?
